title: Should a model sound more sure?
hook: A model is right 70% of the time. What confidence should it claim?

knows: what it means for a model to be right a share of the time
that a model can state a probability
doesNotKnow: that a stated confidence can be scored for honesty
that the squared-gap score is lowest when the stated confidence equals the true hit rate

misconception: A model that sounds more sure is better.
objective: The learner can explain that under the squared-gap (Brier) score the best confidence to state is the true hit rate, so both overconfidence and underconfidence raise the score.

claims.text: Right on 14 of 20, stating r every time, the average squared gap is 0.7(1 − r)² + 0.3r²: 0.250 at 90%, 0.210 at 70%, 0.250 at 50%.
claims.source: avgGap() in Demo.tsx over the 20 outcomes (exact, not sampled); node: 0.2500, 0.2100, 0.2500. Also 0.300 at 100%, 0.220 at 60% and 80%.

claims.text: The average squared gap is lowest exactly at r = 0.7, the hit rate; at 90% each miss costs 0.81, and at 50% each hit costs 0.25.
The squared-gap score is the Brier score, and it is proper: on average it is minimised by stating the true probability, so it cannot be gamed by sounding surer or by hedging.
claims.source: Brier 1950, 'Verification of forecasts expressed in terms of probability', Monthly Weather Review 78(1); Gneiting & Raftery 2007, 'Strictly proper scoring rules, prediction, and estimation', JASA 102(477) (the Brier/quadratic score is strictly proper).

claims.text: The model and its 14 of 20 record are a toy, labelled on the stage; which answers are wrong comes from an untuned mulberry32(1) shuffle and does not change the score.
claims.source: Brief 39 in company/domains/briefs/ai.md (which used 'right 70% of the time'; the toy fixes exactly 14 of 20 so the stage average equals the expected value).

recall.question: A weather app says '90% chance of rain' on days when it rains only 6 times in 10. What would improve its squared-gap (Brier) score?
options: Nothing: it is right more often than not
recall.why: The squared-gap score is lowest when the stated chance matches how often it actually rains. Claiming 90% when the rate is 60% is overconfident and costs on every dry day.
